response.sql: WITH excluded AS (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-'), per_patient AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(CAST(l.ALP AS REAL) / l.GPT) AS avg_alp_gpt_ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.ID NOT IN (SELECT ID FROM excluded) GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT COALESCE(p.SEX, '') AS SEX, AVG(pp.avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(pp.avg_alp_gpt_ratio) AS avg_alp_gpt_ratio FROM per_patient pp JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = pp.ID GROUP BY COALESCE(p.SEX, '');

assumptions.assumption: A blank SEX is either NULL or an empty string, and both are grouped together as one group.
Each record's ALP ÷ GPT ratio is computed as a real-valued division (CAST to REAL) to avoid integer truncation; a zero GPT yields NULL and is ignored by AVG.
Patients with no lab records contribute nothing, because they have no per-patient averages to include. Patients with no non-null PT values are likewise left out of the PT average.
The U-PRO exclusion is an exact match on the string '-', with no trimming or case handling.
